advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a liveness anchor proving the slow shim ran (e.g. assert wall-clock elapsed >= _SLOW_UPDATE_REF_SECS around the acquire, or have the shim write a marker file the test asserts exists) so test_ref_backend_roundtrip_survives_a_slow_local_git_call cannot pass when the shim is not invoked.
evidence: Test intent per docstring: "Acquire and release still succeed when each ``git update-ref`` takes longer than the production bound" (tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py:142-143)
Shim sleeps only on the update-ref branch: "if 'update-ref' in sys.argv[1:]:" then "time.sleep({_SLOW_UPDATE_REF_SECS})" (lines 151-152)

No elapsed-time floor or shim-invocation marker is asserted anywhere in the test — the only assertions are `assert oid` (line 159) and the exit-code check `assert gone.returncode != 0` (line 167), both of which pass whether or not the sleep executed. ABSENCE rationale: with no liveness anchor on the producer (the slow shim), the acquire/release would complete quickly and every assertion would still pass if the shim never ran, so the test cannot distinguish 'roundtrip tolerated a 5.6s update-ref' from 'the slow path was never exercised'.
search_files for 'time' in the test shows time.sleep only inside the generated shim source (lines 150, 152); no timing assertion in the test body.
advisory.finding: test_ref_backend_roundtrip_survives_a_slow_local_git_call never asserts that the slow git shim actually ran, so it can pass vacuously if the PATH shim is not invoked (PATH not honored, shim not executable, or the `update-ref` arg match misses the real invocation) — the test would then report that the roundtrip 'survives a slow local git call' in a world where no slow call ever occurred.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Wrap the acquire in a timer and assert the delay was actually incurred, e.g.:
    import time
    start = time.monotonic()
    oid = advisory_lock.acquire_pass_lock("pass-slow", tmp_git_repo)
    assert time.monotonic() - start >= _SLOW_UPDATE_REF_SECS, "slow update-ref shim did not run"
or have the shim append to a marker file and assert the marker is non-empty before trusting the roundtrip result.
